findings.pdf_says: GENERAL FORMAT FOR FILE CONTROL ENTRY
findings.why_it_matters: The centred, underlined figure title is a heading on every sibling page (pages 194-196, 198, 199, 201, 203, 204 carry it as `## <u>GENERAL FORMAT ...</u>`); on page 197 it is plain underlined body text, so the heading-based outline and page slicing miss the V-5 SEQUENTIAL/RELATIVE file control entry formats.

findings.markdown_says:
Data Division

                         GENERAL FORMAT FOR DATA DIVISION
findings.why_it_matters: The figure title is buried inside a <pre> block with the running header instead of being a `##` heading like its siblings, so the Data Division general format (V-8) has no heading in the transcription's outline.

findings.pdf_says: BLOCK CONTAINS [integer-1 TO] integer-2 {RECORDS / CHARACTERS} (RECORDS underlined; CHARACTERS printed without underline)
findings.why_it_matters: Underlining added: per §1985:IV.2.1.2 an uppercase word not underlined is optional. The printed BLOCK CONTAINS clause (sequential FD, V-9) leaves CHARACTERS un-underlined (the implicitly selected choice that may be omitted, e.g. BLOCK CONTAINS 80); the markdown makes it a required key word, falsely restrictive syntax. Page 203's transcription of the same clause correctly leaves it plain.

findings.pdf_says: BLOCK CONTAINS [integer-1 TO] integer-2 {RECORDS / CHARACTERS} (RECORDS underlined; CHARACTERS printed without underline)
findings.why_it_matters: Same added underline in the relative-file FD (V-10): CHARACTERS is an optional word in the printed figure (§1985:IV.2.1.2), the markdown marks it a required key word, so BLOCK CONTAINS integer-2 with CHARACTERS omitted reads as illegal.
